1→# Translators Bridge
     2→
     3→**An Unreal Engine plugin that connects your game to The Translators -- a cognitive profiling experience where personality emerges from play, not questionnaires.**
     4→
     5→Players answer eight questions. Their choices, timing, and hesitation patterns generate a deterministic cognitive profile exportable as USD. The same answers always produce the same profile.
     6→
     7→---
     8→
     9→## What's In the Box
    10→
    11→| Component | What It Does |
    12→|-----------|-------------|
    13→| **TranslatorsBridge plugin** | Drop-in UE plugin with Runtime + Editor modules |
    14→| **Question delivery system** | Presents questions, collects answers, tracks behavioral signals |
    15→| **Profile engine** | Generates deterministic cognitive profiles from player responses |
    16→| **USD export** | Profiles export as `.usda` files for pipeline integration |
    17→| **Full UI kit** | Title screen, question display, option buttons, progress indicator, finale screen |
    18→
    19→---
    20→
    21→## Quick Start
    22→
    23→### 1. Enable the Plugin
    24→
    25→1. Copy `Plugins/TranslatorsBridge/` into your project's `Plugins/` folder
    26→2. Open your project in Unreal Editor
    27→3. Go to **Edit > Plugins**, search for "Translators Bridge", and enable it
    28→4. Restart the editor when prompted
    29→
    30→### 2. Add the Bridge to Your Level
    31→
    32→**Option A: Blueprint (recommended)**
    33→
    34→1. Create a new Actor Blueprint
    35→2. Add a **Bridge Component** to it
    36→3. Place the actor in your level
    37→4. In the Details panel, bind the events you need:
    38→
    39→| Event | When It Fires |
    40→|-------|--------------|
    41→| `On Bridge Ready` | Connection established, ready to start |
    42→| `On Question Received` | A new question is ready to display |
    43→| `On Transition Received` | Moving between questions |
    44→| `On Finale Received` | All questions answered, profile ready |
    45→
    46→**Option B: C++ Subsystem (advanced)**
    47→
    48→The plugin provides `UTranslatorsBridgeSubsystem` -- a GameInstance subsystem you can access from anywhere:
    49→
    50→```cpp
    51→#include "TranslatorsBridgeSubsystem.h"
    52→
    53→UTranslatorsBridgeSubsystem* Bridge = GetGameInstance()->GetSubsystem<UTranslatorsBridgeSubsystem>();
    54→Bridge->StartGame();
    55→```
    56→
    57→### 3. Start the Python Backend
    58→
    59→In a terminal, from the project root:
    60→
    61→```bash
    62→python bridge_orchestrator.py
    63→```
    64→
    65→The bridge communicates through files in `~/.translators/`. No network configuration needed.
    66→
    67→---
    68→
    69→## How It Works
    70→
    71→```
    72→  Python Backend                    Unreal Engine
    73→  ──────────────                    ──────────────
    74→  bridge_orchestrator.py     ←→     TranslatorsBridge Plugin
    75→         │                                  │
    76→    Writes questions           Reads questions, shows UI
    77→    to ~/.translators/         Writes answers back
    78→         │                                  │
    79→    Reads answers              Tracks response time,
    80→    Generates profile          hesitation, click patterns
    81→         │                                  │
    82→    Exports .usda              Displays cognitive profile
    83→```
    84→
    85→The bridge uses plain files -- no sockets, no ports, no network setup. It just works.
    86→
    87→---
    88→
    89→## The UI Widgets
    90→
    91→All widgets are fully programmatic -- no Blueprint assets required. They build themselves in C++ and render with The Translators' signature dark-cyan aesthetic.
    92→
    93→| Widget | Purpose |
    94→|--------|---------|
    95→| `W_TitleScreen` | "The Translators" title with pulsing "Press ENTER to begin" prompt |
    96→| `W_ConnectingScreen` | "Connecting to Claude Code..." status display |
    97→| `W_QuestionDisplay` | Question text + answer buttons + depth tier label + progress |
    98→| `W_OptionButton` | Individual answer button with hover/press states |
    99→| `W_ProgressIndicator` | 8-dot progress bar (cyan = done, gold = current, gray = remaining) |
   100→| `W_FinaleScreen` | Full cognitive profile display with traits, scores, and insights |
   101→
   102→### Customizing the Look
   103→
   104→Every color and font comes from `FTranslatorsStyle` -- a registered Slate style set. To override colors without touching code:
   105→
   106→**In Blueprint:** Each widget exposes style properties (Background Color, Text Color, etc.) in the Details panel under **Translators | Style**.
   107→
   108→**In C++:** Override the style set:
   109→
   110→```cpp
   111→#include "TranslatorsStyle.h"
   112→
   113→// Get any named color
   114→FLinearColor Cyan = FTranslatorsStyle::GetColor("Color.Cyan");
   115→
   116→// Get any named font
   117→FSlateFontInfo TitleFont = FTranslatorsStyle::GetFont("Font.Title");
   118→```
   119→
   120→### Color Palette
   121→
   122→| Token | Color | Used For |
   123→|-------|-------|----------|
   124→| `Color.Cyan` | ![#5cffdb](https://via.placeholder.com/12/5cffdb/5cffdb.png) `#5cffdb` | Titles, accents, completed progress |
   125→| `Color.Gold` | ![#ffcc33](https://via.placeholder.com/12/ffcc33/ffcc33.png) `#ffcc33` | Current progress indicator |
   126→| `Color.Background` | Near-black | All screen backgrounds |
   127→| `Color.TextPrimary` | Off-white | Body text |
   128→| `Color.TextDim` | Mid-gray | Subtitles, secondary info |
   129→
   130→### Font Scale
   131→
   132→| Token | Size | Used For |
   133→|-------|------|----------|
   134→| `Font.Title` | 56 | Title screen heading |
   135→| `Font.Heading` | 36 | Finale screen heading |
   136→| `Font.Question` | 24 | Question text |
   137→| `Font.Subtitle` | 18 | Subtitles |
   138→| `Font.Body` | 16 | General text |
   139→| `Font.Caption` | 12 | Labels, headers |
   140→
   141→All fonts use `FCoreStyle` defaults -- DPI-aware, no hardcoded font files.
   142→
   143→---
   144→
   145→## Input
   146→
   147→The title screen accepts **Enter** or **Space** to start. It also supports **Enhanced Input** -- assign a `UInputAction` to the `StartInputAction` property in the Details panel if your project uses the Enhanced Input system.
   148→
   149→Answer buttons are mouse/touch clickable with hover and press feedback.
   150→
   151→---
   152→
   153→## The Cognitive Profile
   154→
   155→After eight questions, the engine generates a profile like this:
   156→
   157→```
   158→DIMENSIONS
   159→───────────────────────────────
   160→cognitive_load       Synthesizer    72%
   161→  Prefers to integrate multiple perspectives
   162→
   163→decision_making      Adaptive       65%
   164→  Shifts approach based on context
   165→
   166→communication        Direct         80%
   167→  Values clarity and conciseness
   168→
   169→INSIGHTS
   170→───────────────────────────────
   171→  Gravitates toward systematic decomposition
   172→  Responds well to structured frameworks
   173→  Shows high tolerance for ambiguity
   174→
   175→[TRANSLATORS:101bfab5]
   176→```
   177→
   178→The checksum at the bottom is deterministic -- same answers always produce the same hash. This is how you verify profile integrity.
   179→
   180→---
   181→
   182→## Project Structure
   183→
   184→```
   185→Plugins/TranslatorsBridge/
   186→├── TranslatorsBridge.uplugin          # Plugin descriptor
   187→├── Resources/Icon128.png              # Plugin icon
   188→├── Content/Widgets/                   # Widget assets
   189→└── Source/
   190→    ├── TranslatorsBridgeRuntime/      # Ships in packaged builds
   191→    │   ├── Public/
   192→    │   │   ├── BridgeTypes.h          # Shared types (questions, profiles, signals)
   193→    │   │   ├── TranslatorsBridgeSubsystem.h  # Main game flow subsystem
   194→    │   │   └── TranslatorsStyle.h     # Slate style system
   195→    │   └── Private/
   196→    │       ├── TranslatorsBridgeSubsystem.cpp
   197→    │       └── TranslatorsStyle.cpp
   198→    └── TranslatorsBridgeEditor/       # Editor-only (file watching, process management)
   199→        ├── Public/
   200→        │   └── BridgeEditorSubsystem.h
   201→        └── Private/
   202→            └── BridgeEditorSubsystem.cpp
   203→
   204→Source/TranslatorsCard/                # Game module (thin relay to plugin)
   205→├── BridgeComponent.h/cpp             # Legacy component (forwards to subsystem)
   206→└── UI/
   207→    ├── W_TitleScreen.h/cpp
   208→    ├── W_ConnectingScreen.h/cpp
   209→    ├── W_QuestionDisplay.h/cpp
   210→    ├── W_OptionButton.h/cpp
   211→    ├── W_ProgressIndicator.h/cpp
   212→    ├── W_FinaleScreen.h/cpp
   213→    └── TranslatorsHUD.h/cpp
   214→```
   215→
   216→---
   217→
   218→## Blueprint API Reference
   219→
   220→### Bridge Component
   221→
   222→| Function | Description |
   223→|----------|-------------|
   224→| `SendAnswer(QuestionId, OptionIndex, ResponseTimeMs)` | Submit the player's answer |
   225→| `SendAcknowledge()` | Tell the backend you're ready for the next question |
   226→| `IsBridgeConnected()` | Check if the Python backend is running |
   227→| `GetCurrentQuestion()` | Get the current question data |
   228→
   229→### Bridge Subsystem
   230→
   231→| Function | Description |
   232→|----------|-------------|
   233→| `StartGame()` | Begin the bridge connection and game session |
   234→| `StopGame()` | End the session and clean up |
   235→| `SubmitAnswer(Answer)` | Submit a structured answer |
   236→| `GetBridgeState()` | Current state (Idle, Connected, QuestionActive, etc.) |
   237→| `GetBehavioralSignals()` | Response timing, hesitation count, detected state |
   238→
   239→### Question Data (`FTranslatorsQuestion`)
   240→
   241→| Property | Type | Description |
   242→|----------|------|-------------|
   243→| `QuestionId` | String | Unique identifier |
   244→| `Text` | String | Question text (supports `\n` for line breaks) |
   245→| `OptionLabels` | String Array | Answer option display text |
   246→| `OptionDirections` | String Array | Semantic direction per option |
   247→| `Index` | Int | Current question number (0-based) |
   248→| `Total` | Int | Total questions in session |
   249→| `DepthLabel` | String | Tier: SURFACE, PATTERNS, FEELINGS, or CORE |
   250→
   251→---
   252→
   253→## Requirements
   254→
   255→- Unreal Engine 5.4+
   256→- Windows (Win64)
   257→- Python 3.x (for the backend orchestrator)
   258→
   259→## License
   260→
   261→MIT
   262→
   263→## Author
   264→
   265→[Joseph Ibrahim](https://github.com/JosephOIbrahim)
   266→

    29→from contextlib import contextmanager
    30→from datetime import datetime
    31→import logging
    32→import os

    53→DEFAULT_BRIDGE_PATH = Path.home() / ".translators"

    59→# ATOMIC FILE I/O
    60→# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    61→
    62→@contextmanager
    63→def _file_lock(file_path: Path, timeout: float = 5.0):
    64→    """Advisory file lock using msvcrt on Windows, fcntl on Unix.
    65→
    66→    Acquires an exclusive lock on a .lock file adjacent to the target.
    67→    Falls back to no-op if locking is unavailable.
    68→    """
    69→    lock_path = file_path.with_suffix(file_path.suffix + ".lock")
    70→    lock_fd = None
    71→    try:
    72→        lock_fd = open(lock_path, "w", encoding="utf-8")

    74→            import msvcrt
    75→            import time
    76→            deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    77→            while True:
    78→                try:
    79→                    msvcrt.locking(lock_fd.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_NBLCK, 1)
    80→                    break
    81→                except OSError:

    84→                        break

    86→        except ImportError:

    89→                fcntl.flock(lock_fd.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)

    96→                try:
    97→                    import msvcrt
    98→                    msvcrt.locking(lock_fd.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_UNLCK, 1)

1→"""
     2→remote_control_bridge.py - REST API wrapper for UE5 Remote Control.
     3→
     4→Wraps the UE5 Remote Control plugin's HTTP API (localhost:30010).
     5→Used by the MCP server (Phase 3) and can be run standalone for testing.
     6→
     7→Result capture: Every script is wrapped to capture stdout and exceptions,
     8→writing results to a temp JSON file that the bridge reads back.
     9→
    10→Usage:
    11→    python remote_control_bridge.py --test    # Run self-test (editor must be running)
    12→    python remote_control_bridge.py --info    # Check if editor is reachable
    13→"""
    14→
    15→import json
    16→import logging
    17→import os
    18→import sys
    19→import time
    20→import argparse
    21→import uuid
    22→from typing import Any, Optional
    23→
    24→import httpx
    25→
    26→from ue_mcp.metrics import metrics
    27→
    28→logger = logging.getLogger("ue5-mcp.bridge")
    29→
    30→BASE_URL = os.environ.get("UE_REMOTE_URL", "http://localhost:30010")
    31→TIMEOUT = 10.0
    32→RESULT_POLL_INTERVAL = 0.2  # seconds between result file checks
    33→RESULT_POLL_TIMEOUT = 10.0  # max seconds to wait for result
    34→MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024  # 10 MB cap on JSON responses
    35→
    36→# Circuit breaker settings
    37→CB_FAILURE_THRESHOLD = 5    # consecutive failures before opening
    38→CB_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT = 30.0  # seconds before half-open retry
    39→CB_HALF_OPEN_MAX = 1        # max concurrent requests in half-open
    40→
    41→# Connection pool settings
    42→POOL_MAX_CONNECTIONS = 10
    43→POOL_MAX_KEEPALIVE = 5
    44→
    45→
    46→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    47→# Circuit Breaker
    48→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    49→
    50→class CircuitBreaker:
    51→    """Simple circuit breaker for UE5 connection resilience.
    52→
    53→    States:
    54→    - CLOSED: normal operation, requests pass through
    55→    - OPEN: failures exceeded threshold, requests fail-fast
    56→    - HALF_OPEN: recovery timeout elapsed, allow one probe request
    57→    """
    58→
    59→    CLOSED = "closed"
    60→    OPEN = "open"
    61→    HALF_OPEN = "half_open"
    62→
    63→    def __init__(self, failure_threshold: int = CB_FAILURE_THRESHOLD,
    64→                 recovery_timeout: float = CB_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT):
    65→        self.failure_threshold = failure_threshold
    66→        self.recovery_timeout = recovery_timeout
    67→        self._state = self.CLOSED
    68→        self._failure_count = 0
    69→        self._last_failure_time = 0.0
    70→
    71→    @property
    72→    def state(self) -> str:
    73→        if self._state == self.OPEN:
    74→            if time.time() - self._last_failure_time >= self.recovery_timeout:
    75→                self._state = self.HALF_OPEN
    76→                logger.info("Circuit breaker -> HALF_OPEN (attempting recovery)")
    77→        return self._state
    78→
    79→    def allow_request(self) -> bool:
    80→        s = self.state
    81→        if s == self.CLOSED:
    82→            return True
    83→        if s == self.HALF_OPEN:
    84→            return True  # allow probe
    85→        return False  # OPEN
    86→
    87→    def record_success(self):
    88→        if self._state in (self.HALF_OPEN, self.OPEN):
    89→            logger.info("Circuit breaker -> CLOSED (connection recovered)")
    90→        self._state = self.CLOSED
    91→        self._failure_count = 0
    92→
    93→    def record_failure(self):
    94→        self._failure_count += 1
    95→        self._last_failure_time = time.time()
    96→        if self._failure_count >= self.failure_threshold:
    97→            if self._state != self.OPEN:
    98→                logger.warning(
    99→                    "Circuit breaker -> OPEN after %d failures (cooldown %.0fs)",
   100→                    self._failure_count, self.recovery_timeout,
   101→                )
   102→            self._state = self.OPEN
   103→
   104→    def fail_fast_error(self) -> dict:
   105→        wait = max(0, self.recovery_timeout - (time.time() - self._last_failure_time))
   106→        return {
   107→            "result": None,
   108→            "output": "",
   109→            "error": f"Circuit breaker OPEN — UE5 editor unreachable after {self._failure_count} "
   110→                     f"consecutive failures. Retry in {wait:.0f}s, or restart the editor.",
   111→        }
   112→
   113→
   114→def _make_temp_dir() -> str:
   115→    """Create and return the shared temp directory for UE scripts."""
   116→    import tempfile
   117→    d = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "ue_mcp_scripts")
   118→    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
   119→    return d
   120→
   121→
   122→def _wrap_code(code: str, result_file: str) -> str:
   123→    """Wrap user code with stdout capture and result file output.
   124→
   125→    The wrapper:
   126→    1. Redirects stdout to a StringIO buffer
   127→    2. Executes the user code
   128→    3. Writes {"output": captured_stdout, "error": null} to result_file
   129→    4. On exception, writes {"output": partial_stdout, "error": traceback_str}
   130→    """
   131→    # Escape the result path for embedding in Python string
   132→    safe_path = result_file.replace("\\", "/")
   133→    return f'''
   134→import sys as _sys, io as _io, traceback as _tb, json as _json
   135→
   136→_buf = _io.StringIO()
   137→_old_stdout = _sys.stdout
   138→_sys.stdout = _buf
   139→_error = None
   140→try:
   141→{_indent(code)}
   142→except Exception:
   143→    _error = _tb.format_exc()
   144→finally:
   145→    _sys.stdout = _old_stdout
   146→    _out = _buf.getvalue()
   147→    with open("{safe_path}", "w", encoding="utf-8") as _rf:
   148→        _json.dump({{"output": _out, "error": _error}}, _rf)
   149→'''
   150→

1→"""
     2→UE5 MCP Server - Gives Claude Code native tool access to the Unreal Editor.
     3→
     4→Communicates with UE5 via the Remote Control plugin REST API (localhost:30010).
     5→Runs as an MCP server over stdio transport using FastMCP.
     6→
     7→Usage (registered via `claude mcp add`):
     8→    python ue_mcp/mcp_server.py
     9→    # or via entry point:
    10→    ue-mcp
    11→"""
    12→
    13→import atexit
    14→import glob
    15→import sys
    16→import os
    17→import json
    18→import logging
    19→import tempfile
    20→
    21→# Ensure the ue-bridge root is importable (for remote_control_bridge)
    22→_parent_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    23→if _parent_dir not in sys.path:
    24→    sys.path.insert(0, _parent_dir)
    25→
    26→from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
    27→from remote_control_bridge import AsyncUnrealRemoteControl, BASE_URL
    28→from ue_mcp.__version__ import __version__
    29→from ue_mcp.metrics import metrics
    30→from ue_mcp.tools import register_all_tools
    31→
    32→logging.basicConfig(
    33→    level=logging.INFO,
    34→    format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(name)s: %(message)s",
    35→    stream=sys.stderr,
    36→)
    37→logger = logging.getLogger("ue5-mcp")
    38→
    39→# Create server and bridge
    40→server = FastMCP("unreal-engine")
    41→ue = AsyncUnrealRemoteControl()
    42→
    43→# Register all tool modules
    44→register_all_tools(server, ue)
    45→
    46→
    47→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    48→# Graceful shutdown
    49→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    50→
    51→def _cleanup():
    52→    """Clean up resources on exit."""
    53→    # Close httpx clients
    54→    try:
    55→        ue.close()
    56→    except Exception:
    57→        pass
    58→
    59→    # Remove stale temp files from ue_mcp_scripts
    60→    tmp_dir = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "ue_mcp_scripts")
    61→    if os.path.isdir(tmp_dir):
    62→        stale = glob.glob(os.path.join(tmp_dir, "*.py")) + glob.glob(os.path.join(tmp_dir, "*.json"))
    63→        removed = 0
    64→        for f in stale:
    65→            try:
    66→                os.unlink(f)
    67→                removed += 1
    68→            except OSError:
    69→                pass
    70→        if removed:
    71→            logger.info("Cleanup: removed %d temp files from %s", removed, tmp_dir)
    72→
    73→atexit.register(_cleanup)
    74→
    75→
    76→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    77→# Tools defined here (need access to `ue` and `metrics` instances)
    78→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    79→
    80→@server.tool(
    81→    name="ue_status",
    82→    description="Check if the UE5 editor is running and the Remote Control API is reachable.",
    83→    annotations={
    84→        "readOnlyHint": True,
    85→        "destructiveHint": False,
    86→        "idempotentHint": True,
    87→    },
    88→)
    89→async def status() -> str:
    90→    """Returns connection status and editor info if available."""
    91→    connected = await ue.is_connected()
    92→    if connected:
    93→        try:
    94→            info = await ue.info()
    95→            return json.dumps({
    96→                "connected": True,
    97→                "version": __version__,
    98→                "info": info,
    99→            }, indent=2)
   100→        except Exception as e:
   101→            return json.dumps({
   102→                "connected": True,
   103→                "version": __version__,
   104→                "info_error": str(e),
   105→            }, indent=2)
   106→    return json.dumps({
   107→        "connected": False,
   108→        "version": __version__,
   109→        "message": f"UE5 editor not reachable at {BASE_URL}. Start the editor with RemoteControl plugin enabled.",
   110→    }, indent=2)
   111→
   112→
   113→@server.tool(
   114→    name="ue_health_check",
   115→    description=(
   116→        "Get bridge health: version, uptime, circuit breaker state, "
   117→        "request metrics (counts, latencies, error rates). "
   118→        "Use this to diagnose connection issues."
   119→    ),
   120→    annotations={
   121→        "readOnlyHint": True,
   122→        "destructiveHint": False,
   123→        "idempotentHint": True,
   124→    },
   125→)
   126→async def health_check() -> str:
   127→    """Comprehensive health report for the UE5 bridge."""
   128→    connected = await ue.is_connected()
   129→    cb_state = ue._cb.state if hasattr(ue, "_cb") else "unknown"
   130→
   131→    snap = metrics.snapshot()
   132→
   133→    return json.dumps({
   134→        "version": __version__,
   135→        "connected": connected,
   136→        "base_url": BASE_URL,
   137→        "circuit_breaker": cb_state,
   138→        "uptime_s": snap["uptime_s"],
   139→        "counters": snap["counters"],
   140→        "latencies": snap["latencies"],
   141→    }, indent=2)
   142→
   143→
   144→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   145→# Startup
   146→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   147→
   148→def _startup_checks():
   149→    """Run pre-flight checks and log startup info."""
   150→    logger.info("ue-bridge v%s starting (stdio transport)", __version__)

1→"""Actor manipulation tools for UE5 MCP server."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import json
     6→import logging
     7→
     8→from ._validation import sanitize_class_name, sanitize_label, sanitize_object_path, make_error
     9→
    10→logger = logging.getLogger("ue5-mcp.tools.actors")
    11→
    12→
    13→def register(server, ue):
    14→    @server.tool(
    15→        name="ue_spawn_actor",
    16→        description="Spawn an actor in the UE5 editor by class name at a given location.",
    17→        annotations={
    18→            "readOnlyHint": False,
    19→            "destructiveHint": False,
    20→            "idempotentHint": False,
    21→        },
    22→    )
    23→    async def spawn_actor(
    24→        class_name: str = "StaticMeshActor",
    25→        x: float = 0.0,
    26→        y: float = 0.0,
    27→        z: float = 0.0,
    28→        rx: float = 0.0,
    29→        ry: float = 0.0,
    30→        rz: float = 0.0,
    31→        label: str | None = None,
    32→    ) -> str:
    33→        """Spawn an actor. class_name can be a UE class like StaticMeshActor, PointLight, CameraActor, etc."""
    34→        if err := sanitize_class_name(class_name):
    35→            return make_error(err)
    36→        if label is not None:
    37→            if err := sanitize_label(label):
    38→                return make_error(err)
    39→
    40→        result = await ue.spawn_actor(
    41→            class_name,
    42→            location=(x, y, z),
    43→            rotation=(rx, ry, rz),
    44→            label=label,
    45→        )
    46→        return json.dumps(result, indent=2)
    47→
    48→    @server.tool(
    49→        name="ue_delete_actor",
    50→        description="Delete an actor from the level by its object path.",
    51→        annotations={
    52→            "readOnlyHint": False,
    53→            "destructiveHint": True,
    54→            "idempotentHint": True,
    55→        },
    56→    )
    57→    async def delete_actor(actor_path: str) -> str:
    58→        """Delete an actor by its full object path (e.g. /Game/Maps/MainLevel.MainLevel:PersistentLevel.Cube_1)."""
    59→        if err := sanitize_object_path(actor_path, "actor_path"):
    60→            return make_error(err)
    61→
    62→        result = await ue.delete_actor(actor_path)
    63→        return json.dumps(result, indent=2)
    64→
    65→    @server.tool(
    66→        name="ue_list_actors",
    67→        description="List all actors in the current level, optionally filtered by class name.",
    68→        annotations={
    69→            "readOnlyHint": True,
    70→            "destructiveHint": False,
    71→            "idempotentHint": True,
    72→        },
    73→    )
    74→    async def list_actors(class_filter: str | None = None) -> str:

  1211→# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  1212→
  1213→def compute_checksum(dimensions: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
  1214→    """
  1215→    Compute deterministic checksum for profile (ThinkingMachines [He2025] compliant).
  1216→
  1217→    FIXED algorithm: Sort alphabetically, serialize, DJB2 hash to 8-char hex.
  1218→    Same inputs ALWAYS produce same output regardless of call order or batch size.
  1219→
  1220→    Args:
  1221→        dimensions: Dict of profile dimensions
  1222→
  1223→    Returns:
  1224→        8-character hex checksum
  1225→    """
  1226→    # FIXED: Sort alphabetically for determinism
  1227→    sorted_dims = sorted(dimensions.items())
  1228→
  1229→    # FIXED: Serialize format TRL_v1|key:value|key:value|...
  1230→    serialized = "TRL_v1|" + "|".join(f"{k}:{v}" for k, v in sorted_dims)
  1231→
  1232→    # FIXED: DJB2 hash algorithm (batch-invariant)
  1233→    hash_val = 5381
  1234→    for char in serialized:
  1235→        hash_val = ((hash_val << 5) + hash_val) + ord(char)
  1236→        hash_val &= 0xFFFFFFFF  # Keep 32-bit
  1237→
  1238→    return format(hash_val, '08x')
  1239→
  1240→
  1241→def generate_exec_anchor(
  1242→    checksum: str,
  1243→    expert: str = "Direct",
  1244→    paradigm: str = "Cortex",
  1245→    altitude: str = "Ground",
  1246→    verbosity: str = "standard",
  1247→    think_depth: str = "standard"
  1248→) -> str:
  1249→    """
  1250→    Generate ThinkingMachines-compliant [EXEC:...] anchor.
  1251→
  1252→    Format: [EXEC:{checksum}|{expert}|{paradigm}|{altitude}|{verbosity}|{think_depth}]
  1253→
  1254→    This anchor encodes the routing parameters used for this response,
  1255→    enabling reproducibility verification per ThinkingMachines [He2025].
  1256→
  1257→    Args:
  1258→        checksum: Profile checksum (8 hex chars)
  1259→        expert: ADHD_MoE expert (Validator|Scaffolder|Restorer|Refocuser|Celebrator|Socratic|Direct)
  1260→        paradigm: Cortex (hierarchical) or Mycelium (emergent)
  1261→        altitude: 30000ft|15000ft|5000ft|Ground
  1262→        verbosity: minimal|standard|detailed
  1263→        think_depth: minimal|standard|deep|ultradeep
  1264→
  1265→    Returns:
  1266→        Formatted [EXEC:...] anchor string
  1267→    """
  1268→    return f"[EXEC:{checksum}|{expert}|{paradigm}|{altitude}|{verbosity}|{think_depth}]"
  1269→
  1270→
  1271→def parse_exec_anchor(anchor: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, str]]:
  1272→    """
  1273→    Parse [EXEC:...] anchor to extract routing parameters.
  1274→
  1275→    Args:
  1276→        anchor: The [EXEC:...] anchor string
  1277→
  1278→    Returns:
  1279→        Dict with checksum, expert, paradigm, altitude, verbosity, think_depth
  1280→        or None if parsing fails
  1281→    """
  1282→    match = re.match(r'\[EXEC:([^|]+)\|([^|]+)\|([^|]+)\|([^|]+)\|([^|]+)\|([^\]]+)\]', anchor)
  1283→    if not match:
  1284→        return None
  1285→
  1286→    return {
  1287→        "checksum": match.group(1),
  1288→        "expert": match.group(2),
  1289→        "paradigm": match.group(3),
  1290→        "altitude": match.group(4),
  1291→        "verbosity": match.group(5),
  1292→        "think_depth": match.group(6)
  1293→    }
  1294→
  1295→
  1296→def get_expert_from_signals(signals: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
  1297→    """
  1298→    Route to ADHD_MoE expert based on behavioral signals.
  1299→
  1300→    FIXED PRIORITY (first match wins - ThinkingMachines compliant):
  1301→    1. Validator  - frustrated, RED, caps, negative
  1302→    2. Scaffolder - overwhelmed, stuck, too_many
  1303→    3. Restorer   - depleted, ORANGE, post-crash
  1304→    4. Refocuser  - distracted, tangent_over
  1305→    5. Celebrator - task_complete, milestone
  1306→    6. Socratic   - exploring, high_energy, what if
  1307→    7. Direct     - focused, hyperfocused, flow (DEFAULT)
  1308→
  1309→    Args:
  1310→        signals: Behavioral signals dict
  1311→
  1312→    Returns:
  1313→        Expert name string
  1314→    """
  1315→    detected_state = signals.get("detected_state", "focused")
  1316→    burnout_level = signals.get("burnout_level", "GREEN")
  1317→    rapid_clicks = signals.get("rapid_click_count", 0)
  1318→    hesitations = signals.get("hesitation_count", 0)
  1319→
  1320→    # FIXED priority order - NEVER reorder or skip
  1321→
  1322→    # Priority 1: Validator
  1323→    if detected_state == "frustrated" or burnout_level == "RED" or rapid_clicks > 3:
  1324→        return "Validator"
  1325→
  1326→    # Priority 2: Scaffolder
  1327→    if detected_state in ("stuck", "overwhelmed") or hesitations > 2:
  1328→        return "Scaffolder"

Perfect! Now I have a comprehensive understanding. Let me create a structured summary document:

## Complete Architecture Overview: UE-Bridge Project

### Project Summary

**The Translators Bridge** is a sophisticated Unreal Engine 5.7 plugin system that connects cognitive profiling questionnaires to Claude Code via a file-based bridge protocol with USD (Universal Scene Description) native transport. The system generates deterministic personality profiles exportable as USDA files for AI consumption, integrating behavioral signal collection, MoE (Mixture of Experts) routing, and professional-grade UI components.

**Version:** 2.1.0  
**Language:** C++ (UE5 plugin), Python 3.11+ (orchestration & MCP)  
**Engine:** Unreal Engine 5.4+ (5.7 tested)  
**Platform:** Windows (Win64), optional cross-platform support

---

## 1. Architecture Layers

### Layer 1: Game Flow Bridge (File-Based Protocol)

**Components:**
- `bridge_orchestrator.py` (33KB) — Main orchestration engine
- `usd_bridge.py` (52KB) — USD-native file I/O with JSON fallback

**How It Works:**
```
Python Backend                    Unreal Engine (5.7)
────────────────                  ───────────────────
bridge_orchestrator.py     ←→     TranslatorsBridge Plugin
       │                                  │
  Writes questions           Reads questions, shows UI
  to ~/.translators/         Writes answers back
       │                                  │
  Reads answers              Tracks response time,
  Generates profile          hesitation, click patterns
       │                                  │
  Exports .usda              Displays cognitive profile
```

**Files Used:**
- `~/.translators/bridge_state.usda` — State machine (USD VariantSets)
- `~/.translators/state.json` — Fallback for questions (JSON)
- `~/.translators/answer.json` — Fallback for answers
- `~/.translators/cognitive_profile.usda` — Final profile (USD)
- `~/.translators/heartbeat.json` — Liveness indicator (5s interval)

**Protocol Modes:**
1. **USD-Native (v2.0.0):** VariantSets for state machine, references to profile substrate
2. **JSON Fallback (v1.0.0):** Simple JSON files, backward compatible

---

### Layer 2: C++ Plugin System (TranslatorsBridge)

**Plugin Structure:**
```
Plugins/TranslatorsBridge/
├── TranslatorsBridge.uplugin (v2.1.0 descriptor)
├── Resources/Icon128.png
└── Source/
    ├── TranslatorsBridgeRuntime/      (ships in packaged builds)
    │   ├── Public/
    │   │   ├── BridgeTypes.h          # Enums, structs, delegates
    │   │   ├── TranslatorsBridgeSubsystem.h  # GameInstanceSubsystem (main)
    │   │   └── TranslatorsStyle.h     # Slate style system
    │   └── Private/
    │       ├── TranslatorsBridgeSubsystem.cpp  # Core state machine logic
    │       └── TranslatorsStyle.cpp            # Style registration
    └── TranslatorsBridgeEditor/       (editor-only, Phase 4)
        ├── Public/
        │   └── BridgeEditorSubsystem.h
        └── Private/
            └── BridgeEditorSubsystem.cpp
```

**Key Types (BridgeTypes.h):**

| Type | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `ETranslatorsBridgeState` | State machine: Idle, WaitingForBridge, Connected, QuestionActive, AnswerPending, Transitioning, Complete, Error |
| `FTranslatorsQuestion` | Structured question: id, text, scene, 3 options with directions |
| `FTranslatorsProfile` | Generated profile: 8 dimensions (0-1.0 each) + insights |
| `FBehavioralSignals` | Tracking: response_time_ms, hesitation_count, rapid_clicks, detected_state, burnout_level |
| `EDepthTier` | Question progression: SURFACE (Q1-2), PATTERNS (Q3-4), FEELINGS (Q5-6), CORE (Q7-8) |

**Subsystem (UTranslatorsBridgeSubsystem):**
- Inherits: `UGameInstanceSubsystem`, `FTickableGameObject`
- Runs at 10Hz polling (configurable)
- Owns file I/O, state machine, behavioral tracking
- Broadcasts 6 typed delegates:
  - `OnBridgeReady` → Python orchestrator connected
  - `OnQuestionReady` → New question available
  - `OnTransitionReady` → Scene transition
  - `OnProfileComplete` → Profile ready
  - `OnBridgeError` → Error occurred
  - `OnUsdProfileUpdated` → USD file changed on disk

---

### Layer 3: Blueprint UI Components

**C++ UI Widgets (no Blueprint assets required):**

| Widget | Purpose | Location |
|--------|---------|----------|
| `W_TitleScreen` | "The Translators" title + Enter/Space start prompt | `Source/TranslatorsCard/UI/` |
| `W_ConnectingScreen` | "Connecting to Claude Code..." status | Dynamic, appears during bridge connection |
| `W_QuestionDisplay` | Question text + 3 option buttons + progress (1/8) + depth label | Main interactive widget |
| `W_OptionButton` | Individual answer button with hover/press states | Created dynamically by W_QuestionDisplay |
| `W_ProgressIndicator` | 8-dot progress bar (cyan=done, gold=current, gray=remaining) | Display-only |
| `W_FinaleScreen` | Full cognitive profile with traits, scores, insights, checksum | End of session |
| `TranslatorsHUD` | Root HUD canvas, coordinates all widgets | Sets up widget hierarchy |

**Styling System (TranslatorsStyle.h):**
- Slate-style system (no DPI-relative hardcoding)
- Named colors: `Color.Cyan (#5cffdb)`, `Color.Gold (#ffcc33)`, `Color.Background`, `Color.TextPrimary`, `Color.TextDim`
- Named fonts: `Font.Title (56)`, `Font.Heading (36)`, `Font.Question (24)`, `Font.Body (16)`, `Font.Caption (12)`
- All customizable via Details panel under "Translators | Style"

**Input Handling:**
- Title screen: **Enter** or **Space** to start
- Enhanced Input System support (optional `StartInputAction`)
- Option buttons: Mouse/touch click with visual feedback

---

### Layer 4: MCP Server for Claude Code

**Location:** `ue_mcp/` directory

**Components:**
- `mcp_server.py` — FastMCP server entry point, stdio transport
- `remote_control_bridge.py` — HTTP wrapper for UE5 Remote Control API (localhost:30010)
- `metrics.py` — Telemetry (request counts, latencies, circuit breaker state)
- `tools/` — 8 tool modules registered with MCP

**Tool Modules:**

| Module | Tools Provided | Purpose |
|--------|---|---------|
| `actors.py` | `spawn_actor`, `delete_actor`, `list_actors`, `set_transform`, `get_properties` | Actor manipulation |
| `properties.py` | `set_property`, `get_property`, `list_properties` | Property access |
| `python_exec.py` | `ue_execute_python` | Execute Python in UE editor context |
| `assets.py` | `load_asset`, `list_assets`, `find_references` | Asset management |
| `level.py` | `get_level_info`, `load_level` | Level operations |
| `mograph.py` | Motion graphics/procedural modeling tools | Advanced animation |

def compute_checksum(dimensions):
    # FIXED: Sort alphabetically for determinism
    sorted_dims = sorted(dimensions.items())
    
    # FIXED: Serialize format TRL_v1|key:value|...
    serialized = "TRL_v1|" + "|".join(f"{k}:{v}" for k, v in sorted_dims)
    
    # FIXED: DJB2 hash algorithm (batch-invariant, He2025 compliant)
    hash_val = 5381
    for char in serialized:
        hash_val = ((hash_val << 5) + hash_val) + ord(char)
    
    return format(hash_val, '08x')  # 8-char hex
```

## 13. Key Design Principles

1. **Determinism First:** Same inputs → same outputs always, enabling reproducible AI routing
2. **File-Based Bridge:** No network setup, works on all systems with filesystem
3. **USD Composition Semantics:** VariantSets as state machine, references for profile substrate
4. **No Blueprint Assets:** All UI programmatic (C++), fits in plugin package
5. **Graceful Degradation:** USD → JSON fallback if pxr unavailable
6. **Circuit Breaker Resilience:** Connection failures don't cascade
7. **Atomic File I/O:** Race conditions prevented via temp + replace
8. **Backward Compatible:** v1 JSON protocol still supported, v2 USD preferred

## 3. Profile Generation Engine

**Determinism Guarantee:**
```
Same answers ALWAYS produce same checksum.
Algorithm: DJB2 hash(sorted_dimensions)
```

**Checksum Computation (lines 1213-1238):**
```python
def compute_checksum(dimensions):
    # FIXED: Sort alphabetically for determinism
    sorted_dims = sorted(dimensions.items())
    
    # FIXED: Serialize format TRL_v1|key:value|...
    serialized = "TRL_v1|" + "|".join(f"{k}:{v}" for k, v in sorted_dims)
    
    # FIXED: DJB2 hash algorithm (batch-invariant, He2025 compliant)
    hash_val = 5381
    for char in serialized:
        hash_val = ((hash_val << 5) + hash_val) + ord(char)
    
    return format(hash_val, '08x')  # 8-char hex
```

## 6. Python Bridge Orchestrator

**bridge_orchestrator.py (800+ lines)**

**Entry Point:**
```bash
python bridge_orchestrator.py           # USD mode (auto-fallback to JSON)
python bridge_orchestrator.py --json    # Force JSON mode

```

**Game Flow State Machine:**
```
START
  ↓
PrintBanner + CreateBridgeDir
  ↓
HeartbeatWriter.start()  ← Background thread writes /heartbeat.json every 5s
  ↓
For each question (0-7):
  ├─ write_question() → bridge_state.usda or state.json
  ├─ print_question() → Terminal display
  ├─ wait_for_answer() → Poll with adaptive backoff (50ms → 500ms)
  │   ├─ Read answer.json or bridge_state.usda
  │   ├─ Validate answer (question_id, option_index match)
  │   └─ On timeout (300s) → Error, exit
  ├─ Extract behavioral signals (response_time_ms, timestamps)
  └─ Print answer received
  ↓
Call profile_generator.buildProfile(answers)
  ↓
Export profile → cognitive_profile.usda
  ↓
Heartbeat.stop()
  ↓
END

```

**Polling Strategy (Adaptive Backoff):**
```python
poll_interval = 0.05  # Start at 50ms
while waiting_for_answer:
    sleep(poll_interval)
    if answer_file_exists():
        parse_and_return()
    else:
        poll_interval = min(poll_interval * 1.5, 0.5)  # Cap at 500ms
```

## 12. Agentic Capabilities

### What Claude Code Can Do (via MCP)

**Perception:**

**Python Execution:**

**Asset Management:**

**Level Operations:**
- Get level info
- Load levels

**Limitations:**
- No direct C++ compilation (would require Editor rebuild)
- Remote Control API only (no editor UI automation)
- 10MB response cap per request
- Circuit breaker prevents thundering herd (5 failures → 30s cooldown)

### Current Behavioral Tracking (In-Game)

The subsystem collects:
- **response_time_ms** — Time from question display to answer
- **hesitation_count** — Multiple option hovers without clicking
- **rapid_click_count** — Rapid sequential clicks
- **detected_state** — Inferred from above (focused, distracted, frustrated, stuck, overwhelmed, etc.)
- **burnout_level** — GREEN (healthy), YELLOW (caution), ORANGE (depleted), RED (critical)

Used for **ADHD_MoE routing** in profile generation.

## 13. Key Design Principles

1. **Determinism First:** Same inputs → same outputs always, enabling reproducible AI routing
2. **File-Based Bridge:** No network setup, works on all systems with filesystem
3. **USD Composition Semantics:** VariantSets as state machine, references for profile substrate
4. **No Blueprint Assets:** All UI programmatic (C++), fits in plugin package
5. **Graceful Degradation:** USD → JSON fallback if pxr unavailable
6. **Circuit Breaker Resilience:** Connection failures don't cascade
7. **Atomic File I/O:** Race conditions prevented via temp + replace
8. **Backward Compatible:** v1 JSON protocol still supported, v2 USD preferred

---

## 14. Workflow: Game → Profile → Claude

```
1. Player starts in UE5
   ↓
2. BridgeComponent or Subsystem calls StartGame()
   ↓
3. File watcher begins polling ~/.translators/
   ↓
4. Python orchestrator.py writes Q1 to bridge_state.usda
   ↓
5. UE5 reads, displays W_QuestionDisplay with 3 buttons
   ↓
6. Player clicks option, W_QuestionDisplay fires OnAnswerSelected
   ↓
7. Subsystem captures response_time_ms, writes answer to bridge_state.usda
   ↓
8. Python reads answer, increments signals, continues
   ↓
9. Repeat for Q2-Q8
   ↓
10. Python generates profile, computes checksum, exports cognitive_profile.usda
   ↓
11. W_FinaleScreen displays profile + checksum [TRANSLATORS:xxxxx]
   ↓
12. Claude Code (via MCP) reads cognitive_profile.usda
   ↓
13. Claude extracts dimensions, routes to ADHD_MoE expert, tailors response
```

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code when working with the UnrealEngine_Bridge project.

## Project Overview

**UnrealEngine_Bridge** is an agentic AI bridge connecting Claude Code to Unreal Engine 5.7. It enables AI-driven workflows where Claude can perceive, reason about, and manipulate UE5 scenes through MCP tools, a file-based bridge protocol, and the Remote Control API.

Forked from TranslatorsGame/ue-bridge. The original focused on cognitive profiling game delivery; this fork focuses on **expanding agentic capabilities** -- making Claude a more capable, autonomous collaborator inside Unreal Engine.

## Commands

```bash
# UE5 project
# Open UnrealEngine_Bridge.uproject in UE 5.7 Editor

# Python bridge
python bridge_orchestrator.py          # Start bridge (USD mode, JSON fallback)
python bridge_orchestrator.py --json   # Force JSON mode
python bridge_orchestrator.py --test   # Write test question and exit

# MCP server
pip install -e ".[dev]"               # Install with dev dependencies
python -m ue_mcp.mcp_server           # Start MCP server (stdio)

# Tests
python -m pytest tests/ -v            # All tests
python -m pytest tests/test_usd_bridge.py -v    # USD bridge tests
python -m pytest tests/test_circuit_breaker.py   # Resilience tests
```

## Architecture

```
UnrealEngine_Bridge/
├── Plugins/
│   ├── UEBridge/                    # Core bridge plugin
│   │   └── Source/
│   │       ├── UEBridgeRuntime/     # Ships in builds: subsystem, types, UI, style
│   │       └── UEBridgeEditor/      # Editor-only: file watching, process mgmt
│   └── ViewportPerception/          # Viewport capture + metadata for AI perception
├── Source/
│   └── UnrealEngineBridge/          # Game module (thin relay to plugin)
│       ├── BridgeComponent.*        # Legacy BP-bindable component
│       └── UI/                      # Slate widgets (title, questions, profile)
├── ue_mcp/                          # MCP server for Claude Code
│   ├── mcp_server.py               # FastMCP entry point (stdio)
│   ├── remote_control_bridge.py     # HTTP wrapper for UE5 Remote Control API
│   ├── metrics.py                   # Telemetry + circuit breaker
│   └── tools/                       # 8 tool modules
│       ├── actors.py                # spawn, delete, list, transform, properties
│       ├── properties.py            # get/set/list UObject properties
│       ├── python_exec.py           # Execute Python in UE editor context
│       ├── assets.py                # load, list, find references
│       ├── level.py                 # level info, load level
│       ├── mograph.py               # Motion graphics / procedural modeling
│       ├── blueprints.py            # compile, get pins
│       └── perception.py            # Viewport screenshots + bridge state
├── bridge_orchestrator.py           # Python game flow orchestration
├── usd_bridge.py                    # USD/JSON file I/O, profile generation
├── remote_control_bridge.py         # Standalone RC API wrapper
└── tests/                           # pytest suite
```

### Communication Stack

```
Claude Code  <--MCP (stdio)-->  ue_mcp/mcp_server.py
                                      |
                               HTTP (localhost:30010)
                                      |
                              UE5 Remote Control API
                                      |
                              UE5 Editor / Runtime
```

### File-Based Bridge Protocol

```
Python Backend                    UE5 Plugin (UEBridgeSubsystem)
─────────────────                 ────────────────────────────────
Writes to ~/.translators/   ←→   Polls ~/.translators/ at 10Hz
  bridge_state.usda                 Reads questions, writes answers
  state.json (fallback)             Tracks behavioral signals
  cognitive_profile.usda            Displays UI widgets
  heartbeat.json (5s)
```

## Key Files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `Plugins/UEBridge/Source/UEBridgeRuntime/Public/BridgeTypes.h` | All structs, enums, delegates |
| `Plugins/UEBridge/Source/UEBridgeRuntime/Public/UEBridgeSubsystem.h` | Main subsystem (state machine, polling) |
| `Plugins/UEBridge/Source/UEBridgeRuntime/Public/UEBridgeStyle.h` | Slate style system |
| `ue_mcp/tools/*.py` | MCP tool implementations |
| `usd_bridge.py` | USD I/O, checksum, profile generation |
| `bridge_orchestrator.py` | Game flow state machine |

## Agentic Capabilities (Current)

### What Claude Can Do via MCP

| Capability | Tools | Status |
|-----------|-------|--------|
| **Perceive** viewport | `ue_viewport_percept` | Working |
| **Spawn/delete** actors | `spawn_actor`, `delete_actor`, `list_actors` | Working |
| **Transform** actors | `set_transform` | Working |
| **Read/write** properties | `get_property`, `set_property`, `list_properties` | Working |
| **Execute** Python in editor | `ue_execute_python` | Working |
| **Manage** assets | `load_asset`, `list_assets`, `find_references` | Working |
| **Control** levels | `get_level_info`, `load_level` | Working |
| **Compile** Blueprints | `compile_blueprint`, `get_blueprint_pins` | Working |

### Agentic Gaps (Priority Improvements)

These are the capabilities that would make Claude a significantly better UE5 collaborator:

1. **Scene understanding** -- Claude can capture viewport but lacks structured scene graph queries (get all actors of type, spatial queries, hierarchy traversal)
2. **Material/shader editing** -- No tools for creating or modifying materials, Material Instances, or shader parameters
3. **Animation control** -- No Sequencer integration, no ability to play/scrub/keyframe animations
4. **Blueprint graph editing** -- Can compile but can't create/wire nodes programmatically
5. **Build/cook pipeline** -- No tools for packaging, cooking, or build validation
6. **Multi-frame perception** -- Single viewport snapshot; no video/sequence capture or diff-based change detection
7. **Console command execution** -- Limited; needs structured output parsing
8. **Plugin hot-reload** -- Changes to C++ require full editor restart

## Resilience

- **Circuit breaker**: CLOSED -> OPEN (5 failures) -> HALF_OPEN (30s) -> CLOSED
- **Connection pooling**: 10 max, 5 keepalive
- **Adaptive timeout**: 10s default
- **Atomic file I/O**: tempfile + os.replace (NTFS-safe)
- **Advisory locking**: msvcrt on Windows

## What You Can Change Freely

- MCP tool implementations (ue_mcp/tools/)
- Python bridge logic
- Test coverage
- Build configuration
- Bug fixes, performance

## What Requires Discussion

- New MCP tool categories
- Changes to bridge protocol (affects both Python and C++ sides)
- UEBridgeSubsystem state machine changes
- New C++ plugin modules

## Code Patterns

### Adding a New MCP Tool

1. Create `ue_mcp/tools/your_tool.py`
2. Define functions decorated with `@mcp.tool()`
3. Use `AsyncUnrealRemoteControl` for UE5 communication
4. Register in `ue_mcp/mcp_server.py`
5. Add tests in `tests/`

### Remote Control API Pattern

```python
from remote_control_bridge import AsyncUnrealRemoteControl

async with AsyncUnrealRemoteControl() as rc:
    result = await rc.execute_python("unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.get_all_level_actors()")
```

### C++ Subsystem Pattern

```cpp
// Access from anywhere
UUEBridgeSubsystem* Bridge = GetGameInstance()->GetSubsystem<UUEBridgeSubsystem>();
Bridge->OnQuestionReady.AddDynamic(this, &AMyActor::HandleQuestion);
```

                              UE5 Editor / Runtime
```

### File-Based Bridge Protocol

```
Python Backend                    UE5 Plugin (UEBridgeSubsystem)
─────────────────                 ────────────────────────────────
Writes to ~/.translators/   ←→   Polls ~/.translators/ at 10Hz
  bridge_state.usda                 Reads questions, writes answers
  state.json (fallback)             Tracks behavioral signals
  cognitive_profile.usda            Displays UI widgets
  heartbeat.json (5s)
```

## Key Files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `Plugins/UEBridge/Source/UEBridgeRuntime/Public/BridgeTypes.h` | All structs, enums, delegates |
| `Plugins/UEBridge/Source/UEBridgeRuntime/Public/UEBridgeSubsystem.h` | Main subsystem (state machine, polling) |
| `Plugins/UEBridge/Source/UEBridgeRuntime/Public/UEBridgeStyle.h` | Slate style system |
| `ue_mcp/tools/*.py` | MCP tool implementations |
| `usd_bridge.py` | USD I/O, checksum, profile generation |
| `bridge_orchestrator.py` | Game flow state machine |

## Agentic Capabilities (Current)

### What Claude Can Do via MCP

| Capability | Tools | Status |
|-----------|-------|--------|
| **Perceive** viewport | `ue_viewport_percept` | Working |
| **Spawn/delete** actors | `spawn_actor`, `delete_actor`, `list_actors` | Working |
| **Transform** actors | `set_transform` | Working |
| **Read/write** properties | `get_property`, `set_property`, `list_properties` | Working |
| **Execute** Python in editor | `ue_execute_python` | Working |
| **Manage** assets | `load_asset`, `list_assets`, `find_references` | Working |
| **Control** levels | `get_level_info`, `load_level` | Working |
| **Compile** Blueprints | `compile_blueprint`, `get_blueprint_pins` | Working |

### Agentic Gaps (Priority Improvements)

These are the capabilities that would make Claude a significantly better UE5 collaborator:

1. **Scene understanding** -- Claude can capture viewport but lacks structured scene graph queries (get all actors of type, spatial queries, hierarchy traversal)
2. **Material/shader editing** -- No tools for creating or modifying materials, Material Instances, or shader parameters
3. **Animation control** -- No Sequencer integration, no ability to play/scrub/keyframe animations
4. **Blueprint graph editing** -- Can compile but can't create/wire nodes programmatically
5. **Build/cook pipeline** -- No tools for packaging, cooking, or build validation
6. **Multi-frame perception** -- Single viewport snapshot; no video/sequence capture or diff-based change detection
7. **Console command execution** -- Limited; needs structured output parsing
8. **Plugin hot-reload** -- Changes to C++ require full editor restart

## Resilience

- **Circuit breaker**: CLOSED -> OPEN (5 failures) -> HALF_OPEN (30s) -> CLOSED
- **Connection pooling**: 10 max, 5 keepalive
- **Adaptive timeout**: 10s default
- **Atomic file I/O**: tempfile + os.replace (NTFS-safe)
- **Advisory locking**: msvcrt on Windows

## What You Can Change Freely

- MCP tool implementations (ue_mcp/tools/)
- Python bridge logic
- Test coverage
- Build configuration
- Bug fixes, performance

## What Requires Discussion

- New MCP tool categories
- Changes to bridge protocol (affects both Python and C++ sides)
- UEBridgeSubsystem state machine changes
- New C++ plugin modules

## Code Patterns

### Adding a New MCP Tool

1. Create `ue_mcp/tools/your_tool.py`
2. Define functions decorated with `@mcp.tool()`
3. Use `AsyncUnrealRemoteControl` for UE5 communication
4. Register in `ue_mcp/mcp_server.py`
5. Add tests in `tests/`

### Remote Control API Pattern

```python
from remote_control_bridge import AsyncUnrealRemoteControl

async with AsyncUnrealRemoteControl() as rc:
    result = await rc.execute_python("unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.get_all_level_actors()")
```

### C++ Subsystem Pattern

```cpp
// Access from anywhere
UUEBridgeSubsystem* Bridge = GetGameInstance()->GetSubsystem<UUEBridgeSubsystem>();
Bridge->OnQuestionReady.AddDynamic(this, &AMyActor::HandleQuestion);
```

# Translators Bridge

**An Unreal Engine plugin that connects your game to The Translators -- a cognitive profiling experience where personality emerges from play, not questionnaires.**

Players answer eight questions. Their choices, timing, and hesitation patterns generate a deterministic cognitive profile exportable as USD. The same answers always produce the same profile.

---

## What's In the Box

| Component | What It Does |
|-----------|-------------|
| **UEBridge plugin** | Drop-in UE plugin with Runtime + Editor modules |
| **Question delivery system** | Presents questions, collects answers, tracks behavioral signals |
| **Profile engine** | Generates deterministic cognitive profiles from player responses |
| **USD export** | Profiles export as `.usda` files for pipeline integration |
| **Full UI kit** | Title screen, question display, option buttons, progress indicator, finale screen |

---

## Quick Start

### 1. Enable the Plugin

1. Copy `Plugins/UEBridge/` into your project's `Plugins/` folder
2. Open your project in Unreal Editor
3. Go to **Edit > Plugins**, search for "Translators Bridge", and enable it
4. Restart the editor when prompted

### 2. Add the Bridge to Your Level

**Option A: Blueprint (recommended)**

1. Create a new Actor Blueprint
2. Add a **Bridge Component** to it
3. Place the actor in your level
4. In the Details panel, bind the events you need:

| Event | When It Fires |
|-------|--------------|
| `On Bridge Ready` | Connection established, ready to start |
| `On Question Received` | A new question is ready to display |
| `On Transition Received` | Moving between questions |
| `On Finale Received` | All questions answered, profile ready |

**Option B: C++ Subsystem (advanced)**

The plugin provides `UUEBridgeSubsystem` -- a GameInstance subsystem you can access from anywhere:

```cpp
#include "UEBridgeSubsystem.h"

UUEBridgeSubsystem* Bridge = GetGameInstance()->GetSubsystem<UUEBridgeSubsystem>();
Bridge->StartGame();
```

### 3. Start the Python Backend

In a terminal, from the project root:

```bash
python bridge_orchestrator.py
```

The bridge communicates through files in `~/.translators/`. No network configuration needed.

---

## How It Works

```
  Python Backend                    Unreal Engine
  ──────────────                    ──────────────
  bridge_orchestrator.py     ←→     UEBridge Plugin
         │                                  │
    Writes questions           Reads questions, shows UI
    to ~/.translators/         Writes answers back
         │                                  │
    Reads answers              Tracks response time,
    Generates profile          hesitation, click patterns
         │                                  │
    Exports .usda              Displays cognitive profile
```

The bridge uses plain files -- no sockets, no ports, no network setup. It just works.

---

## The UI Widgets

All widgets are fully programmatic -- no Blueprint assets required. They build themselves in C++ and render with The Translators' signature dark-cyan aesthetic.

| Widget | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `W_TitleScreen` | "The Translators" title with pulsing "Press ENTER to begin" prompt |
| `W_ConnectingScreen` | "Connecting to Claude Code..." status display |
| `W_QuestionDisplay` | Question text + answer buttons + depth tier label + progress |
| `W_OptionButton` | Individual answer button with hover/press states |
| `W_ProgressIndicator` | 8-dot progress bar (cyan = done, gold = current, gray = remaining) |
| `W_FinaleScreen` | Full cognitive profile display with traits, scores, and insights |

### Customizing the Look

Every color and font comes from `FTranslatorsStyle` -- a registered Slate style set. To override colors without touching code:

**In Blueprint:** Each widget exposes style properties (Background Color, Text Color, etc.) in the Details panel under **Translators | Style**.

**In C++:** Override the style set:

```cpp
#include "TranslatorsStyle.h"

// Get any named color
FLinearColor Cyan = FTranslatorsStyle::GetColor("Color.Cyan");

// Get any named font
FSlateFontInfo TitleFont = FTranslatorsStyle::GetFont("Font.Title");
```

### Color Palette

| Token | Color | Used For |
|-------|-------|----------|
| `Color.Cyan` | ![#5cffdb](https://via.placeholder.com/12/5cffdb/5cffdb.png) `#5cffdb` | Titles, accents, completed progress |
| `Color.Gold` | ![#ffcc33](https://via.placeholder.com/12/ffcc33/ffcc33.png) `#ffcc33` | Current progress indicator |
| `Color.Background` | Near-black | All screen backgrounds |
| `Color.TextPrimary` | Off-white | Body text |
| `Color.TextDim` | Mid-gray | Subtitles, secondary info |

### Font Scale

| Token | Size | Used For |
|-------|------|----------|
| `Font.Title` | 56 | Title screen heading |
| `Font.Heading` | 36 | Finale screen heading |
| `Font.Question` | 24 | Question text |
| `Font.Subtitle` | 18 | Subtitles |
| `Font.Body` | 16 | General text |
| `Font.Caption` | 12 | Labels, headers |

All fonts use `FCoreStyle` defaults -- DPI-aware, no hardcoded font files.

---

## Input

The title screen accepts **Enter** or **Space** to start. It also supports **Enhanced Input** -- assign a `UInputAction` to the `StartInputAction` property in the Details panel if your project uses the Enhanced Input system.

Answer buttons are mouse/touch clickable with hover and press feedback.

---

## The Cognitive Profile

After eight questions, the engine generates a profile like this:

```
DIMENSIONS
───────────────────────────────
cognitive_load       Synthesizer    72%
  Prefers to integrate multiple perspectives

decision_making      Adaptive       65%
  Shifts approach based on context

communication        Direct         80%
  Values clarity and conciseness

INSIGHTS
───────────────────────────────
  Gravitates toward systematic decomposition
  Responds well to structured frameworks
  Shows high tolerance for ambiguity

[TRANSLATORS:101bfab5]
```

The checksum at the bottom is deterministic -- same answers always produce the same hash. This is how you verify profile integrity.

---

## Project Structure

```
Plugins/UEBridge/
├── UEBridge.uplugin          # Plugin descriptor
├── Resources/Icon128.png              # Plugin icon
├── Content/Widgets/                   # Widget assets
└── Source/
    ├── UEBridgeRuntime/      # Ships in packaged builds
    │   ├── Public/
    │   │   ├── BridgeTypes.h          # Shared types (questions, profiles, signals)
    │   │   ├── UEBridgeSubsystem.h  # Main game flow subsystem
    │   │   └── TranslatorsStyle.h     # Slate style system
    │   └── Private/
    │       ├── UEBridgeSubsystem.cpp
    │       └── TranslatorsStyle.cpp
    └── UEBridgeEditor/       # Editor-only (file watching, process management)
        ├── Public/
        │   └── BridgeEditorSubsystem.h
        └── Private/
            └── BridgeEditorSubsystem.cpp

Source/UnrealEngineBridge/                # Game module (thin relay to plugin)
├── BridgeComponent.h/cpp             # Legacy component (forwards to subsystem)
└── UI/
    ├── W_TitleScreen.h/cpp
    ├── W_ConnectingScreen.h/cpp
    ├── W_QuestionDisplay.h/cpp
    ├── W_OptionButton.h/cpp
    ├── W_ProgressIndicator.h/cpp
    ├── W_FinaleScreen.h/cpp
    └── TranslatorsHUD.h/cpp
```

---

## Blueprint API Reference

### Bridge Component

| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `SendAnswer(QuestionId, OptionIndex, ResponseTimeMs)` | Submit the player's answer |
| `SendAcknowledge()` | Tell the backend you're ready for the next question |
| `IsBridgeConnected()` | Check if the Python backend is running |
| `GetCurrentQuestion()` | Get the current question data |

### Bridge Subsystem

| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `StartGame()` | Begin the bridge connection and game session |
| `StopGame()` | End the session and clean up |
| `SubmitAnswer(Answer)` | Submit a structured answer |
| `GetBridgeState()` | Current state (Idle, Connected, QuestionActive, etc.) |
| `GetBehavioralSignals()` | Response timing, hesitation count, detected state |

### Question Data (`FTranslatorsQuestion`)

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `QuestionId` | String | Unique identifier |
| `Text` | String | Question text (supports `\n` for line breaks) |
| `OptionLabels` | String Array | Answer option display text |
| `OptionDirections` | String Array | Semantic direction per option |
| `Index` | Int | Current question number (0-based) |
| `Total` | Int | Total questions in session |
| `DepthLabel` | String | Tier: SURFACE, PATTERNS, FEELINGS, or CORE |

---

- Unreal Engine 5.4+
- Windows (Win64)
- Python 3.x (for the backend orchestrator)

content.content:
1→"""
     2→UE5 MCP Server - Gives Claude Code native tool access to the Unreal Editor.
     3→
     4→Communicates with UE5 via the Remote Control plugin REST API (localhost:30010).
     5→Runs as an MCP server over stdio transport using FastMCP.
     6→
     7→Usage (registered via `claude mcp add`):
     8→    python ue_mcp/mcp_server.py
     9→    # or via entry point:
    10→    ue-mcp
    11→"""
    12→
    13→import atexit
    14→import glob
    15→import sys
    16→import os
    17→import json
    18→import logging
    19→import tempfile
    20→
    21→# Ensure the ue-bridge root is importable (for remote_control_bridge)
    22→_parent_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    23→if _parent_dir not in sys.path:
    24→    sys.path.insert(0, _parent_dir)
    25→
    26→from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
    27→from remote_control_bridge import AsyncUnrealRemoteControl, BASE_URL
    28→from ue_mcp.__version__ import __version__
    29→from ue_mcp.metrics import metrics
    30→from ue_mcp.tools import register_all_tools
    31→
    32→logging.basicConfig(
    33→    level=logging.INFO,
    34→    format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(name)s: %(message)s",
    35→    stream=sys.stderr,
    36→)
    37→logger = logging.getLogger("ue5-mcp")
    38→
    39→# Create server and bridge
    40→server = FastMCP("unreal-engine")
    41→ue = AsyncUnrealRemoteControl()
    42→
    43→# Register all tool modules
    44→register_all_tools(server, ue)
    45→
    46→
    47→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    48→# Graceful shutdown
    49→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    50→
    51→def _cleanup():
    52→    """Clean up resources on exit."""
    53→    # Close httpx clients
    54→    try:
    55→        ue.close()
    56→    except Exception:
    57→        pass
    58→
    59→    # Remove stale temp files from ue_mcp_scripts
    60→    tmp_dir = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "ue_mcp_scripts")
    61→    if os.path.isdir(tmp_dir):
    62→        stale = glob.glob(os.path.join(tmp_dir, "*.py")) + glob.glob(os.path.join(tmp_dir, "*.json"))
    63→        removed = 0
    64→        for f in stale:
    65→            try:
    66→                os.unlink(f)
    67→                removed += 1
    68→            except OSError:
    69→                pass
    70→        if removed:
    71→            logger.info("Cleanup: removed %d temp files from %s", removed, tmp_dir)
    72→
    73→atexit.register(_cleanup)
    74→
    75→
    76→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    77→# Tools defined here (need access to `ue` and `metrics` instances)
    78→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    79→
    80→@server.tool(
    81→    name="ue_status",
    82→    description="Check if the UE5 editor is running and the Remote Control API is reachable.",
    83→    annotations={
    84→        "readOnlyHint": True,
    85→        "destructiveHint": False,
    86→        "idempotentHint": True,
    87→    },
    88→)
    89→async def status() -> str:
    90→    """Returns connection status and editor info if available."""
    91→    connected = await ue.is_connected()
    92→    if connected:
    93→        try:
    94→            info = await ue.info()
    95→            return json.dumps({
    96→                "connected": True,
    97→                "version": __version__,
    98→                "info": info,
    99→            }, indent=2)
   100→        except Exception as e:
   101→            return json.dumps({
   102→                "connected": True,
   103→                "version": __version__,
   104→                "info_error": str(e),
   105→            }, indent=2)
   106→    return json.dumps({
   107→        "connected": False,
   108→        "version": __version__,
   109→        "message": f"UE5 editor not reachable at {BASE_URL}. Start the editor with RemoteControl plugin enabled.",
   110→    }, indent=2)
   111→
   112→
   113→@server.tool(
   114→    name="ue_health_check",
   115→    description=(
   116→        "Get bridge health: version, uptime, circuit breaker state, "
   117→        "request metrics (counts, latencies, error rates). "
   118→        "Use this to diagnose connection issues."
   119→    ),
   120→    annotations={
   121→        "readOnlyHint": True,
   122→        "destructiveHint": False,
   123→        "idempotentHint": True,
   124→    },
   125→)
   126→async def health_check() -> str:
   127→    """Comprehensive health report for the UE5 bridge."""
   128→    connected = await ue.is_connected()
   129→    cb_state = ue._cb.state if hasattr(ue, "_cb") else "unknown"
   130→
   131→    snap = metrics.snapshot()
   132→
   133→    return json.dumps({
   134→        "version": __version__,
   135→        "connected": connected,
   136→        "base_url": BASE_URL,
   137→        "circuit_breaker": cb_state,
   138→        "uptime_s": snap["uptime_s"],
   139→        "counters": snap["counters"],
   140→        "latencies": snap["latencies"],
   141→    }, indent=2)
   142→
   143→
   144→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   145→# Startup
   146→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   147→
   148→def _startup_checks():
   149→    """Run pre-flight checks and log startup info."""
   150→    logger.info("ue-bridge v%s starting (stdio transport)", __version__)
   151→    logger.info("UE5 Remote Control endpoint: %s", BASE_URL)
   152→
   153→    # Verify temp dir is writable
   154→    tmp_dir = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "ue_mcp_scripts")
   155→    try:
   156→        os.makedirs(tmp_dir, exist_ok=True)
   157→        test_file = os.path.join(tmp_dir, "_startup_check.tmp")
   158→        with open(test_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   159→            f.write("ok")
   160→        os.unlink(test_file)
   161→    except OSError as e:
   162→        logger.warning("Temp directory not writable (%s): %s", tmp_dir, e)
   163→
   164→    logger.info("Startup checks passed — ready for connections")
   165→
   166→
   167→def main():
   168→    """Entry point for the MCP server."""
   169→    _startup_checks()
   170→    server.run(transport="stdio")
   171→
   172→
   173→if __name__ == "__main__":
   174→    main()
   175→

1→"""Input validation and security helpers for UE5 MCP tools.
     2→
     3→Provides:
     4→- AST-based Python code sandboxing for execute_python
     5→- String sanitization for actor labels, class names, paths
     6→- Path validation for UE content paths and blueprint paths
     7→"""
     8→
     9→from __future__ import annotations
    10→
    11→import ast
    12→import re
    13→from typing import Optional
    14→
    15→# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    16→# PYTHON CODE SANDBOX
    17→# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    18→
    19→# Modules that must never be imported in editor Python
    20→BLOCKED_MODULES = frozenset({
    21→    "subprocess", "shutil", "socket", "http.server", "xmlrpc",
    22→    "ctypes", "multiprocessing", "signal", "pty", "pipes",
    23→    "webbrowser", "antigravity", "turtle", "tkinter",
    24→    "smtplib", "ftplib", "telnetlib", "poplib", "imaplib",
    25→    "nntplib", "xmlrpc.server",
    26→})
    27→
    28→# Attribute accesses that are dangerous even on allowed modules
    29→BLOCKED_ATTRS = frozenset({
    30→    "system",       # os.system
    31→    "popen",        # os.popen
    32→    "exec",         # builtins.exec (as attr)
    33→    "eval",         # builtins.eval (as attr)
    34→    "execfile",
    35→    "spawn",        # os.spawn*
    36→    "startfile",    # os.startfile
    37→    "rmtree",       # shutil.rmtree
    38→    "rmdir",        # os.rmdir
    39→    "remove",       # os.remove
    40→    "unlink",       # os.unlink / Path.unlink
    41→    "rename",       # os.rename
    42→    "replace",      # os.replace
    43→    "makedirs",     # os.makedirs (outside project)
    44→    "chown",
    45→    "chmod",
    46→    "kill",         # os.kill
    47→})
    48→
    49→# Functions that must never appear as Call targets
    50→BLOCKED_BUILTINS = frozenset({
    51→    "exec", "eval", "compile", "__import__", "breakpoint",
    52→})
    53→
    54→
    55→class CodeValidationError(Exception):
    56→    """Raised when submitted code fails sandbox validation."""
    57→    pass
    58→
    59→
    60→def validate_python_code(code: str) -> Optional[str]:
    61→    """Validate Python code for safety before execution in UE5.
    62→
    63→    Returns None if safe, or an error message string if blocked.
    64→    """
    65→    # Parse the AST — syntax errors are caught here
    66→    try:
    67→        tree = ast.parse(code)
    68→    except SyntaxError as e:
    69→        return f"Syntax error: {e.msg} (line {e.lineno})"
    70→
    71→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
    72→        # Block dangerous imports
    73→        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
    74→            for alias in node.names:
    75→                mod_root = alias.name.split(".")[0]
    76→                if alias.name in BLOCKED_MODULES or mod_root in BLOCKED_MODULES:
    77→                    return f"Blocked import: '{alias.name}' is not allowed in editor scripts"
    78→
    79→        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
    80→            if node.module:
    81→                mod_root = node.module.split(".")[0]
    82→                if node.module in BLOCKED_MODULES or mod_root in BLOCKED_MODULES:
    83→                    return f"Blocked import: 'from {node.module}' is not allowed in editor scripts"
    84→
    85→        # Block dangerous attribute access (e.g., os.system, shutil.rmtree)
    86→        elif isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
    87→            if node.attr in BLOCKED_ATTRS:
    88→                # Check if it's on a known-dangerous module
    89→                if isinstance(node.value, ast.Name) and node.value.id in ("os", "shutil", "pathlib"):
    90→                    return f"Blocked operation: '{node.value.id}.{node.attr}' is not allowed"
    91→
    92→        # Block dangerous builtin calls
    93→        elif isinstance(node, ast.Call):
    94→            func = node.func
    95→            if isinstance(func, ast.Name) and func.id in BLOCKED_BUILTINS:
    96→                return f"Blocked builtin: '{func.id}()' is not allowed in editor scripts"
    97→
    98→    return None
    99→
   100→
   101→# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   102→# STRING SANITIZATION
   103→# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   104→
   105→# Valid UE identifier: alphanumeric, underscores, hyphens, spaces, dots
   106→_SAFE_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r'^[\w\s\-\.()]+$', re.UNICODE)
   107→
   108→# Valid UE class name: PascalCase identifier, no special chars
   109→_SAFE_CLASS_RE = re.compile(r'^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$')
   110→
   111→# Valid UE content path: /Game/... or /Engine/... with safe chars
   112→_SAFE_PATH_RE = re.compile(r'^/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_/\-\.]*$')
   113→
   114→# Valid UE object path (includes : and . for subobject addressing)
   115→_SAFE_OBJECT_PATH_RE = re.compile(r'^/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_/\-\.\:]*$')
   116→
   117→# Property names: alphanumeric, underscores
   118→_SAFE_PROPERTY_RE = re.compile(r'^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$')
   119→
   120→
   121→def sanitize_label(label: str, param_name: str = "label") -> Optional[str]:
   122→    """Validate an actor label. Returns error message or None if valid."""
   123→    if not label:
   124→        return f"{param_name} cannot be empty"
   125→    if len(label) > 256:
   126→        return f"{param_name} too long ({len(label)} chars, max 256)"
   127→    if not _SAFE_LABEL_RE.match(label):
   128→        return f"{param_name} contains invalid characters: only alphanumeric, spaces, hyphens, dots, underscores, and parentheses are allowed"
   129→    return None
   130→
   131→
   132→def sanitize_class_name(class_name: str, param_name: str = "class_name") -> Optional[str]:
   133→    """Validate a UE class name. Returns error message or None if valid."""
   134→    if not class_name:
   135→        return f"{param_name} cannot be empty"
   136→    if len(class_name) > 128:
   137→        return f"{param_name} too long ({len(class_name)} chars, max 128)"
   138→    if not _SAFE_CLASS_RE.match(class_name):
   139→        return f"{param_name} '{class_name}' is not a valid class name (must be alphanumeric/underscores, start with letter)"
   140→    return None
   141→
   142→
   143→def sanitize_content_path(path: str, param_name: str = "path") -> Optional[str]:
   144→    """Validate a UE content path (/Game/..., /Engine/...). Returns error message or None."""
   145→    if not path:
   146→        return f"{param_name} cannot be empty"
   147→    if len(path) > 512:
   148→        return f"{param_name} too long ({len(path)} chars, max 512)"
   149→    if not _SAFE_PATH_RE.match(path):
   150→        return f"{param_name} '{path}' is not a valid content path (must start with / and contain only safe characters)"
   151→    if ".." in path:
   152→        return f"{param_name} contains path traversal sequence '..'"
   153→    return None
   154→
   155→
   156→def sanitize_object_path(path: str, param_name: str = "object_path") -> Optional[str]:
   157→    """Validate a UE object path (includes : and . for subobjects). Returns error message or None."""
   158→    if not path:
   159→        return f"{param_name} cannot be empty"
   160→    if len(path) > 1024:
   161→        return f"{param_name} too long ({len(path)} chars, max 1024)"
   162→    if not _SAFE_OBJECT_PATH_RE.match(path):
   163→        return f"{param_name} '{path}' is not a valid object path"
   164→    if ".." in path.replace("..", ""):  # Allow single dots but not ..
   165→        pass  # UE paths legitimately use dots
   166→    return None
   167→
   168→
   169→def sanitize_property_name(name: str, param_name: str = "property_name") -> Optional[str]:
   170→    """Validate a property name. Returns error message or None."""
   171→    if not name:
   172→        return f"{param_name} cannot be empty"
   173→    if len(name) > 128:
   174→        return f"{param_name} too long ({len(name)} chars, max 128)"
   175→    if not _SAFE_PROPERTY_RE.match(name):
   176→        return f"{param_name} '{name}' is not a valid property name"
   177→    return None
   178→
   179→
   180→def make_error(message: str) -> str:
   181→    """Create a JSON error response string."""
   182→    import json
   183→    return json.dumps({"error": message}, indent=2)
   184→
